post.caption:
Nerve signals travel at up to 120 metres per second, sped up by a fatty myelin sheath that works like insulation on a cable. But the reflex that pulls your hand off a hot pan never reaches your brain first. It goes to the spinal cord, which sends the order straight back down. Your arm is already moving while the message to your brain is still in transit. You do not decide to pull away. You find out that you did.
